title: On-chain Verifiable Risk Capital is deliberately not equivalent to Total Risk Capital
content:
A.2.2.10.1.1.3.2.1.3.1 defines OVRC as the on-chain, verifiable risk-capital components a near-real-time monitor can track, then states plainly: "OVRC is not necessarily equivalent to Total Risk Capital (TRC). A Prime Agent's actual TRC cannot be determined definitively without accounting for off-chain agreements, encumbrances or other relevant conditions affecting capital eligibility or availability."

A.2.2.10.1.1.3.2.1.2.3.1 gives the concrete failure modes: "On-chain data alone... cannot definitively prove the full eligibility and unimpaired availability of a Prime Agent's capital position," naming Prime-initiated off-chain contractual pledges, bridged assets whose "economic value or redeemability... is compromised by issues with their originating bridge," and assets "encumbered by derivative structures or other off-chain commitments."

The important direction is that the error is one-sided. Every named failure mode makes visible capital *less* usable than it appears, so OVRC systematically overstates rather than understates a Prime's true position. A monitor reading only chain state is therefore not conservative — it is optimistic, which is the wrong bias for a solvency control.

Naming the residual gap rather than claiming on-chain verifiability is what justifies keeping a human attestation regime alongside automation. A.2.2.10.1.1.3.2.1.2.3.1 extends this even to the fully-automated future state: the TRC Report "may remain necessary to cover elements of TRC verification that are not fully able to be automated or require explicit Prime Agent declaration."
description: OVRC is what an autonomous monitor can see; off-chain pledges, impaired bridged assets and derivative encumbrances can make real TRC lower, so the gap must be closed by Prime attestation.
